record.paper_title: Open Problems in Data-Sharing Peer-to-Peer Systems
record.original_question: Is there a peer-to-peer design that can support server anonymity, meaning that it is difficult to determine which nodes store a given document, while also supporting efficient search for that document without falling back to expensive broadcast-style search?

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, supporting server anonymity and efficient search concurrently remains an open issue.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a peer-to-peer network: a distributed system consisting of a dynamic collection of nodes (peers) that jointly store a set of documents, with each document replicated on some subset of nodes (its "servers"). Users issue queries naming a document, and the system must locate and retrieve a copy. We say that the system provides:

(i) Server anonymity: for any document D in the system, no participant (other than a server of D itself) and no external observer can determine, with non-negligible advantage over random guessing, which nodes store D, even given the ability to issue queries and observe network traffic.

(ii) Efficient search: any document present in the system can be located by a query whose total communication and computation cost is bounded by a polylogarithmic function (or, more weakly, a sublinear function) of the number of nodes N, ruling out flooding/broadcast-style search whose cost is Ω(N).

Design a peer-to-peer protocol (specifying the routing/indexing structure, the placement of documents, and the search procedure) that simultaneously achieves (i) and (ii), or prove that no such protocol exists under a specified adversary model.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on anonymous P2P systems documents a persistent tension between strong server anonymity and efficient (non-broadcast) search: structured DHT-based systems give efficient lookup but expose servers, while anonymity-providing overlays typically incur significant routing overhead. Some hybrid and indirection-based protocols offer partial tradeoffs, but no published design is widely accepted as achieving both strong server anonymity and polylogarithmic search simultaneously. The problem is generally still regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Secure and Privacy-Aware Searching in Peer-to-Peer Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Unstructured P2P networks need efficient search mechanisms and anonymizing P2P networks often means extra cost in transfer efficiency.
status_evidence.claim: Tradeoff between anonymity and search efficiency in P2P remains a recognized challenge.

status_evidence.title: Anonymous P2P - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Anonymity in P2P systems is typically achieved at significant cost to routing/search efficiency.
status_evidence.claim: No widely accepted design achieves both strong server anonymity and efficient (non-broadcast) search.
